questions.q: What is the key operational difference between Firehose and Kinesis Data Streams?
options: Data Streams can only deliver to S3, while Firehose can deliver anywhere
There is no difference — they are two names for the same service
Firehose is fully managed with no shards to provision; Data Streams requires you to size shards and write a consumer
Firehose only works with on-premises data sources
questions.explain: Firehose abstracts away shard management entirely; you point it at a destination and it scales delivery capacity on its own.

questions.q: How does Firehose decide when to flush a buffer to its destination?
options: Whichever of the configured buffer size or buffer interval threshold is reached first
Once per day, on a fixed schedule
Every single record is delivered the instant it arrives, unbuffered
Only when the buffer reaches exactly 1 GB
questions.explain: You configure both a size threshold (MB) and a time threshold (seconds); Firehose flushes as soon as either one is hit.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a supported Firehose destination?
options: Amazon Redshift
DynamoDB
Amazon S3
OpenSearch Service
questions.explain: Firehose delivers to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch Service, Splunk, and HTTP endpoints — DynamoDB is not one of its supported delivery destinations.

questions.q: What can an optional Lambda transformation attached to a delivery stream do?
options: Permanently disable buffering
Reshape, filter, or enrich records in flight before they're delivered
Increase the number of shards on the source stream
Convert the delivery stream into a Kinesis Data Stream
questions.explain: A Lambda transformation runs on each buffered batch before delivery — a common use is converting JSON to Parquet or stripping unneeded fields.

questions.q: Why is Firehose described as 'load and forget' rather than replayable?
options: Firehose deletes source data before it can be delivered
Firehose requires you to manually resend every record
Once a batch is delivered, Firehose doesn't retain it for multiple consumers to re-read later
Firehose only supports a single record per delivery stream
questions.explain: Unlike Data Streams, Firehose has no retention window or concept of independent consumers reading at their own pace — delivered data lives only at its destination.
